research_domain_title: Equal Standing, Blind-Stage Justice, and Equal Access
note: Foundational constitutional principle and institutional spine. Architecture and developing doctrine only — not a finished equal-protection statute. Distinguishes equal rights and equal treatment under law from treating every situation identically. Complements Declaration 'On equality' (rejects equality of outcome) by specifying equal standing, protection, and accountability. No invented access-to-justice or enforcement statistics.
role_in_philosophy: Equal standing is the common standard that makes liberty, ownership, opportunity, and accountability real for every person. Without it, Constitutional Capitalism collapses into privilege for some and unprotected vulnerability for others. It is not engineered sameness of outcomes; it is non-negotiable equality before the Constitution.

foundational_principle.text: Every person stands equal before the Constitution. Neither wealth, office, race, religion, political affiliation, social status, birthplace, celebrity, nor institutional influence shall increase or diminish the protection of the law or the accountability imposed by the law.

relevant_distinctions_rule.text: Equal standing is not identical treatment of every situation regardless of constitutionally relevant differences. The law may legitimately distinguish, for example, between a child and an adult, or between a person convicted after due process and a person who has not been convicted. Status must not determine justice; relevant legal facts may.
examples_of_legitimate_distinctions: age where the law makes age relevant (child vs adult)
professional licensure where the law imposes role-specific duties
identity facts necessary to prove who committed an act
examples_of_illegitimate_influence: wealth buying better protection or weaker accountability
office or institutional influence creating exemption
celebrity or social status altering the standard of justice
neighborhood, birthplace, or group membership as a substitute for evidence

blind_stage_principle.name: The Blind Stage Principle
blind_stage_principle.analogy_note: Inspired by the idea of hearing the performance before seeing the performer — useful as civic philosophy, not as a claim that courts can literally ignore identity in every proceeding.
blind_stage_principle.text: Justice should evaluate conduct before identity whenever constitutionally and practically possible.
blind_stage_principle.iconic_phrase: The Constitution should hear the evidence before it sees the person.
blind_stage_principle.iconic_phrase_caveat: Taken literally, identity is sometimes legally relevant. As guiding philosophy: judge actions before status; measure merit before influence; protect rights equally; hold everyone equally accountable.
do_not_ask_first: How much money do they have?

equality_of_opportunity_and_accountabili.title: Equality of Opportunity, Equality of Accountability
equality_of_opportunity_and_accountabili.closing_rule: No one is above the law. No one is beneath its protection.

reject_privilege_in_every_direction.summary: Reject privilege and reject arbitrary discrimination. The Constitution is the common standard.
reject: special treatment because of political influence
arbitrary discrimination against people because they belong to any particular group

equal_access_requirements.summary: Equality is not only courtroom outcomes. It requires meaningful access, or equality exists only on paper.
equal_access_requirements.note: Access architecture is a design and research agenda — do not invent representation-rate or FOIA-delay statistics.

civic_culture.text: We may differ in our beliefs, backgrounds, occupations, and experiences, but before the Constitution we are fellow citizens first. Our diversity is real; our equality under the law is non-negotiable.
civic_culture.aim: Citizens should stop seeing one another primarily as competing identity groups and instead share a civic identity under a common constitutional standard.

equal_standing_test.title: Equal Standing Test
equal_standing_test.purpose: Screen every proposed law or institutional design for equal application, privilege, disadvantage, clarity, uniform enforcement, official self-exemption, and effects on opportunity versus influence — before acceptance into the framework.

questions.text: Does it create a privileged class?
Does it create a disadvantaged class without constitutional justification?
Is enforcement likely to be uniform?
Does it expand equal opportunity or unequal influence?

relationship_to_declaration.text: Declaration 'On equality' rejects equality of outcome. Equal Standing specifies equality of constitutional footing, protection, opportunity to participate, and accountability. The two are complementary — not contradictory.
